RULE (three halves): (i) a record identified for access locked by ANOTHER file connector => the operation's result depends on the presence or absence of the RETRY phrase; (ii) RETRY present => 'additional attempts may be made to read the record as specified in the rules in 14.7.9, RETRY phrase'; (iii) 'The I-O status is set in accordance with the rules for the RETRY phrase.' VALIDATED: `python scripts/spec/cite.py --check 14.9.30.4 "The I-O status is set in accordance with the rules for the RETRY phrase"` -> OK 14.9.30.4 9); `--check 14.9.30.4 "If the RETRY phrase is not specified or the record is not successfully accessed as specified by the RETRY phrase, the record operation conflict condition exists"` -> OK 14.9.30.4 9); `--check 14.7.9.3 "the result of the evaluation of arithmetic-expression-1 or arithmetic-expression-2 is negative or zero, the statement is unsuccessful"` -> OK 14.7.9.3 4) a); `--check 9.1.13.8 "an attempt to access a record that is currently locked by another file connector"` -> OK 9.1.13.8 1); `--check 9.1.13.8 "The implementor shall specify under what conditions a deadlock is detected"` -> OK 9.1.13.8 2). The four RETRY forms are four different rules with three distinct grounds and one shared landing: no phrase and a negative-or-zero arithmetic-expression-1/-2 are 14.7.9.3 GR4 a); n TIMES is GR4 b) -> GR1 with an exhausted count; FOR n SECONDS is GR4 b) -> GR2, whose timeout period is clamped to this implementation's maximum meaningful value of ZERO (Annex A.1 item 166, docs/CONFORMANCE.md 7), so it makes no attempt either; all four land the closing paragraph's 'appropriate value ... according to the rules for 9.1.13', i.e. the record operation conflict '51' (9.1.13.8 item 1). GR3's FOREVER alone lands '52', the deadlock 9.1.13.8 item 2 leaves the implementor to detect (A.1 item 109): the holder is a connector of the EXECUTING run unit and can never release while this statement runs, so GR3's 'until the input-output operation has been completed' would not terminate. kb/Work PB354. RULE (--check 14.9.41.3 4): 'Data-name-1 or record-key-name-1 shall not be subject to any OCCURS clauses.' The rule has two operand legs (indexed and relative) and they behave differently.
INDEXED LEG -- ENFORCED, but only as a SIDE EFFECT and reported under the WRONG RULE. RecordLayout.OffsetOf bails to null when the item or any ancestor carries OCCURS ('if (p.Occurs is not null) return null;   // subject to OCCURS => no single fixed position'), so KeyIndexByPosition returns null and BindStart emits COBOLNET0862 '<name> neither names a record key nor begins at the leftmost character position of one with a length not greater than that key (ISO 14.9.41 SR6)'. PROBED (out-b1/probe/sr4-occ) with '05 IX-KEY. 10 IX-ELEM PIC X(3) OCCURS 2 TIMES.' and 'START IXF KEY IS = IX-ELEM (1)': rejected with exactly that message. The source IS refused, so no illegal program compiles -- but the message asserts something FALSE about this operand: IX-ELEM(1) DOES begin at IX-KEY's leftmost character position and IS shorter than it. The rule actually violated is SR4; OffsetOf's null collapses two distinct rejection reasons into one sentence, and a user reading it would look for the wrong problem.
RELATIVE LEG -- NO CHECK AT ALL. BindStart's relative arm tests only ReferenceEquals(operand.Item, file.RelativeKeyItem) (that is SR5), which is TRUE for a SUBSCRIPTED reference to the same DataItem. PROBED (same file): with '01 WS-RKT. 05 WS-RK PIC 9(4) OCCURS 3 TIMES.' and 'RELATIVE KEY IS WS-RK', the statement 'START RLF KEY IS = WS-RK (2)' compiles with NO diagnostic. That shape is reachable only through a file control entry that already violates 12.4.5.13.3 SR1 (--check: 'Data-name-1 shall not be subject to any OCCURS clauses') -- and the keyed binder's file screen of that day implemented 12.4.5.13's SR2 (unsigned integer, no P) and SR3 (not within a record of the file) but NOT its SR1, so nothing anywhere in the chain diagnoses it. The two missing checks cover for each other.

Rule: `cite.py --check 14.9.39.3 "if the SET statement is contained in a method within the factory definition of the class, that factory definition shall be described with an IMPLEMENTS clause that references int-1"` -> OK 10) (SR10 d)1.). THE INTERPRETIVE QUESTION, DECIDED FROM THE SPEC: is 'described with an IMPLEMENTS clause that references int-1' a LITERAL claim about the clause's operand list, or the standard's prose for the SS11.4.4 GR2 relation? It is the relation, on four independent grounds. (1) SS11.4.4 GR1: 'The IMPLEMENTS clause specifies the names of the interfaces that are implemented by the factory object of the containing class ACCORDING TO 9.3.11, Interface implementation' - the clause is defined in terms of implementation, not the reverse. (2) SS9.3.8.2.3 rule 5 b)2.a. states the SAME obligation about the SAME objects with the OTHER phrasing: 'if described with the FACTORY phrase, the factory object of the specified class shall be described with an IMPLEMENTS clause that references int-r', where SET SR10 b)1. writes 'the factory object of the specified class shall implement int-1'. Two phrasings, one rule. (3) Annex D (SS D.19.5) paraphrases SS13.18.60.4 GR22 c) - normatively 'the object referenced by this data item shall IMPLEMENT interface-1' - as 'the data item can only be used to reference an object DESCRIBED WITH AN IMPLEMENTS CLAUSE THAT REFERENCES the interface specified': the standard glosses its own rule with the other spelling. The row did not exist when PB329 landed -- an interior '## SEQUENTIAL FILES' heading truncated 14.9.51.4's rule block at GR16, so GR17-GR42 were never in the catalog and PB329's implementer had nothing to close. RULE: 'For a line sequential file, if the record area contains one or more characters that are not in the implementor-defined character set defined for a line sequential file, the execution of the WRITE statement is unsuccessful and the I-O status in the write file connector is set to 71.' cite.py --check 14.9.51.4 'the execution of the WRITE statement is unsuccessful and the I-O status in the write file connector is set to 71' -> OK 14.9.51.4 23). MECHANISM: LineSequentialCharacterSet is the one executable copy of the Annex A.1 item 115 determination (docs/CONFORMANCE.md DOC-A.1-115: every character at or above U+0020 is a member, the C0 controls below it are not), and SequentialConnector.RecordAreaOutsideLineCharacterSet is the one call shape. BOTH write entry points consult it -- Write and WriteAdvancing -- ahead of every shape branch, because the rule is organization-scoped rather than shape-scoped, and ahead of any stream traffic because 9.1.13.10 item 1 requires the record area and the medium to be left unchanged. (There were THREE until kb/Work PB712, 2026-09-06, deleted the third arm, the BEFORE-AND-AFTER write: 14.9.51.2 Format 1 prints ONE ADVANCING operand, so the COBOL-2023 BEFORE AFTER pair is a placement and reaches WriteAdvancing like every other print-control write. The arm count fell; the coverage did not.) The test is CHARACTER-wise, not byte-wise: a national record area is walked two bytes at a time as UTF-16BE, so N"CD"'s 00 43 00 44 is two members and not two control characters. MEASURED on the built cobol.exe before PB329 landed: a line sequential WRITE of a record holding 0x00 reported STATUS=00 and left the byte on the medium; after, STATUS=71 and the file is 0 bytes. Goldens walk 09 (READ, 14.9.30.4 GR16), 71 (WRITE, THIS rule), 71 (REWRITE, 14.9.35.4 GR17d), the unchanged medium, and the set boundary (0x7F -> ordinal 128, 0xFF -> ordinal 256 are members) at 2023, the one edition the LINE SEQUENTIAL organization exists in. kb/Work PB688 (2026-09-05): ORGANIZATION IS LINE SEQUENTIAL is a COBOL-2023 INTRODUCTION - the Foreword's list of the main changes this third edition makes over ISO/IEC 1989:2014 names "Line Sequential file organization", and 9.1.6 / 9.1.7.1 still name exactly three organizations with 9.1.7.2 splitting the sequential one into its record- and line-delimited types. The organization therefore does not exist below 2023 (the pass now rejects it with COBOLNET0900, registry row file-organization-line-sequential-2023), the 2002 and 2014 copies of the golden were deleted as programs no edition below 2023 can express, and this row's editions are 2023 alone.
